big_case.notes: Interim stay, not a merits judgment, but the per curiam announces a categorical rule ('There is no such thing as a "constitutional" major-questions claim') that reaches every jurisdiction-stripping statute preserving only constitutional claims, and it unblocks border-barrier construction across the Big Bend Sector under IIRIRA s.102 waivers. High practical and doctrinal salience for an application; below a merits landmark.

central_claims.basis: Nov 9 order grants the stay pending cert; no summary reversal.
central_claims.claim: The Court will grant an unqualified stay pending certiorari and decline the invitation to summarily reverse.

central_claims.basis: Per curiam's core holding, citing Dalton v. Specter, 511 U.S. at 472-474.
central_claims.claim: Any explanation will center first on s.102(c)(2)(A) and Dalton: an ultra vires statutory claim cannot be recast as a constitutional one to evade the jurisdictional bar.

central_claims.basis: Per curiam rests on jurisdiction plus irreparable harm and Congress's balance of equities; it does not reach s.102(a) scope and does not mention CASA or remedial overbreadth.
central_claims.claim: The explanation will also reject the district court's major-questions narrowing of s.102(a) on statutory merits and find the sector-wide injunction overbroad under Trump v. CASA.
The order will issue Nov 3-9, 2026, after referral to the full Court.

central_claims.basis: Only Jackson noted she would deny; the Court issued an explanatory per curiam.
central_claims.claim: 6-3 lineup with Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson voting to deny (at minimum Sotomayor and Jackson noted), most likely with no authored opinion.
